original_value: Robotic handling systems are increasingly applied in distribution centers. They require little space, provide flexibility in managing varying demand requirements, and are able to work 24/7. This makes them particularly fit for e-commerce operations. This paper reviews new categories of automated and robotic handling systems, such as shuttle-based storage and retrieval systems, shuttle-based compact storage systems, and robotic mobile fulfillment systems. For each system, we categorize the literature in three groups: system analysis, design optimization, and operations planning and control. Our focus is to identify the research issue and operations research modeling methodology adopted to analyze the problem. We find that many new robotic systems and applications have hardly been studied in academic literature, despite their increasing use in practice. Because of unique system features (such as autonomous control, flexible layout, networked and dynamic operation), new models and methods are needed to address the design and operational control challenges for such systems, in particular, for the integration of subsystems. Integrated robotic warehouse systems will form the next category of warehouses. All vital warehouse design, planning, and control logic, such as methods to design layout, storage and order-picking system selection, storage slotting, order batching, picker routing, and picker to order assignment, will have to be revisited for new robotized warehouses.

result.paraphrase: Robotic handling systems are being adopted more and more in distribution centers. They occupy little space, offer flexibility for handling changing demand, and can operate around the clock, making them especially well suited to e-commerce operations. This paper surveys emerging classes of automated and robotic handling systems, including shuttle-based storage and retrieval systems, shuttle-based compact storage systems, and robotic mobile fulfillment systems. For each system, we group the literature into three areas: system analysis, design optimization, and operations planning and control. We aim to identify the research problem and the operations research modeling approach used to study it. We find that many of these new robotic systems and applications have received little attention in the academic literature, despite their growing practical use. Owing to their distinctive features—such as autonomous control, flexible layout, and networked, dynamic operation—new models and methods are required to tackle design and operational control challenges, especially subsystem integration. Integrated robotic warehouse systems will represent the next generation of warehouses. All essential warehouse design, planning, and control logic, including layout design, storage and order-picking system selection, storage slotting, order batching, picker routing, and picker-to-order assignment, must be reconsidered for new robotized warehouses.
